newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigerian blue chips fall in share glut.
newsitem.headline: Nigerian blue chips fall in share glut.

text.p: Blue chip stocks fell in Monday's share trading on the Nigerian stock market as few buyers were active in the glutted market.
The all-share index closed unchanged from Friday at 6982.94 points.

"There were few big buyers about because of the holiday season," one trader said. "These shares should firm up in the new year after the big spenders return and on the expectation of further market reforms."
Conglomerate Lever Brothers led the losers, dropping 20 kobo to 20.00 naira.
Nigerian Breweries went down 10 kobo at 19.30 naira, making earlier forecasts of a price above 20.00 naira by year-end too optimistic, dealers said.
The stock opened at 19.89 naira in January but slid after the company fell on hard times. Recovery took nine months as the shares firmed up only last month after touching 10.00 naira.
Ashaka Cement was 20 kobo lower at 16.50 naira, Afribank ended 15 kobo down at 3.65 naira and Cadbury dropped five kobo to finish at 21.45 naira.
Oil marketers ranked among strong finishers but most ended steady.
Unipetrol, 23 kobo up at 58.78 naira and Union Bank, 20 kobo higher at 6.00 naira were top performers on Monday.
Construction firms Cappa & D'Alberto, G Cappa and Impresit Bakolori added three kobo each on positive investors perception, to 7.36 naira, 11.73 naira and 2.90 naira, respectively.
